question: Why do we say food is like medicine when it comes to preventing long-term illnesses?

options.A: Eating specific foods replaces the need for surgical interventions entirely
options.B: Food items can be prescribed by nurses just like pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Nutrients cure all infectious pathogens without the need for antibiotics
options.D: Dietary choices directly influence the development of conditions like diabetes and hypertension

explanation: You got it! Eating healthy meals helps keep lifestyle diseases like high blood pressure and diabetes away, acting just like preventive medicine.

question: What is the best way to count a patient's respiratory rate accurately without making them change how they breathe?

options.A: Announce loudly that you are starting to count breaths now
options.B: Count respirations discreetly right after taking the radial pulse without moving your hand away
options.C: Place a heavy hand on their chest to feel every rib movement
options.D: Ask them to take ten deep breaths so you can time it

explanation: Smart nursing! Patients often change their breathing if they know you're watching. Transitioning straight from the pulse keeps their breathing natural.

question: Why is coaching the patient to take deep breaths so important during an unsedated sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: It helps relax their belly and pelvic muscles, making it easier to pass the scope.
options.B: It removes the need for lubrication.
options.C: It keeps their blood pressure artificially high.
options.D: It keeps them from swallowing air into their lungs.

explanation: Spot on! When cramps hit, patients naturally tense up. Deep breathing helps them relax those muscles so the procedure goes smoother.

question: Why would a nurse use a Doppler ultrasound gadget during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check the patient's blood glucose level through the skin
options.B: To view the internal valves of veins using radioactive dye
options.C: To measure the exact electrical activity inside the heart muscle
options.D: To detect difficult-to-palpate peripheral pulses using sound waves

explanation: If a pulse is too faint to feel with your fingers, a Doppler uses sound waves to let you hear the 'whoosh' of blood flow loud and clear. Great tool!

question: Why is the skin considered part of the body's primary defense system?

options.A: It produces white blood cells continuously
options.B: It digests harmful toxins entering the body
options.C: It blocks pathogens, chemicals, and physical injury
options.D: It pumps blood to destroy foreign bacteria

explanation: The skin acts as an unbroken physical barrier that stops germs and harsh environmental elements from entering internal tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which surgical method uses metal plates, screws, or rods attached directly to the bone?

options.A: Endoscopic joint debridement
options.B: Closed manual skin traction
options.C: External pin frame fixation
options.D: Open reduction internal fixation

explanation: ORIF involves a surgical incision to place hardware directly on or inside the bone to hold pieces firmly in place. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h7)

question: A patient taking a new blood pressure medication suddenly feels very dizzy and lightheaded when standing up. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to run in place to improve blood circulation
options.B: Administer a stimulant medication to raise the blood pressure
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse immediately
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report the finding

explanation: Dizziness after starting a new blood pressure drug points to orthostatic hypotension, requiring a check of vital signs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: How do bedside nurses play a direct role in improving healthcare quality?

options.A: By conducting all hospital building maintenance and equipment repairs
options.B: By rewriting all state healthcare laws and national medical policies
options.C: By managing the financial investments and budget allocations of the hospital
options.D: By participating in safety committees and suggesting workflow redesigns

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses work hands-on with daily systems, their practical ideas are gold for creating safer workflows and better patient care.

question: Which of these is a normal mental response when someone is in acute grief?

options.A: Total inability to recognize family members forever
options.B: Forgetfulness and poor concentration
options.C: Advanced intellectual enhancement
options.D: Permanent memory loss from brain damage

explanation: Mental fog and trouble focusing are totally normal temporary reactions to high emotional stress. You're doing great!

question: When should you refer a reproductive health patient to a specialist counselor?

options.A: When emotional distress exceeds basic supportive nursing care
options.B: Whenever the patient asks what medication they are taking
options.C: Only after the patient has completed all surgical treatments
options.D: Before the nurse performs any physical assessment

explanation: Spot on! While you provide great initial comfort, deep or complex emotional distress is best handled by mental health specialists.

question: What is the main reason we do routine inventory checks for ward equipment?

options.A: Tracking missing items and keeping emergency tools ready
options.B: Finding out which nurse uses the most supplies
options.C: Permanently locking away expensive diagnostic machines
options.D: Increasing the financial taxes paid by the hospital

explanation: Inventory checks make sure everything we need is present and accounted for before an emergency hits the ward.

question: Why is keeping a look-out for fire hazards trickier in a patient's house compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Private homes are always built using highly flammable wood
options.B: Hospitals have stricter rules against using electricity
options.C: Nurses have no legal authority to check home environments
options.D: Private homes have unpredictable layouts and lack institutional safety systems

explanation: Hospitals have built-in alarms, sprinklers, and standard designs. Every patient's home is different and usually lacks these heavy-duty safety backups.

question: A baby is born with an omphalocele (abdominal organs outside the belly). What is your very first action in the delivery room?

options.A: Give the infant a warm bath to clean them up
options.B: Feed the baby immediately to boost sugar
options.C: Cover the organs with a warm, sterile saline-soaked wrap
options.D: Gently push the organs back inside the tummy

explanation: Protect those exposed organs right away! A warm, moist wrap keeps them safe from infection, injury, and drying out until surgery can happen.

question: What is the main job of the rehab nurse within the healthcare team?

options.A: Prescribing physical therapy exercises and ordering diagnostic imaging tests
options.B: Reinforcing therapy skills and coordinating daily care around the clock
options.C: Providing formal legal counseling for insurance claims
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries to correct bone deformities

explanation: Nurses are with the patient 24/7. We tie all the therapies together and keep the healing going round the clock. You are the heartbeat of the ward!

question: Which of the following is a major financial challenge of using high-fidelity simulation?

options.A: Insurance companies charge high fees for training mannequins
options.B: Mannequins require expensive daily food and water supplies
options.C: High equipment purchase, maintenance, and facility costs
options.D: Students refuse to pay extra fees to use the simulation lab

explanation: Advanced simulators and specialized lab spaces require substantial funding to buy and keep operational. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h7)

question: Why is writing a proposal considered a necessary step for nurse researchers?

options.A: It replaces the need for an official ethics committee review
options.B: It guarantees immediate funding from the government
options.C: It automatically cures the clinical problem being studied
options.D: It ensures the study plan is clear and feasible beforehand

explanation: Working through a proposal forces the researcher to organize their thoughts and check feasibility before spending resources. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is your primary role during an emergency intracardiac injection?

options.A: Performing the needle insertion into the chest wall
options.B: Preparing equipment and monitoring the cardiac rhythm
options.C: Prescribing the correct dosage of emergency drugs
options.D: Documenting the discharge summary for the patient

explanation: Teamwork is key in emergencies! You support the doctor by getting gear ready, timing events, and watching the monitor to see how the patient reacts.

question: Why do we give nitroglycerin to a patient having chest pain from heart disease?

options.A: It dissolves existing blood clots inside the coronary arteries.
options.B: It slows down the electrical signals from the SA node.
options.C: It permanently removes fatty plaque from the artery walls.
options.D: It dilates blood vessels to improve blood flow and lower heart workload.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin relaxes the blood vessels, widening the coronary arteries and making it much easier for the heart to pump.

question: A pregnant mum says cooking smells instantly make her want to throw up. What is happening in her body?

options.A: Immediate closure of the pyloric sphincter from heat
options.B: Direct stimulation of the vomiting center by sensory input
options.C: Rapid absorption of airborne food toxins into the bloodstream
options.D: Sudden drop in systemic blood pressure from food aromas

explanation: Strong smells hit sensory nerves that directly trigger the brain's vomiting center. Pregnant senses are super sharp!

question: Why do hospital cleaners and nurses wipe down bed rails and bedside tables so often?

options.A: Air currents deposit airborne droplets directly onto these objects
options.B: Patients spend most of their recovery time touching these areas
options.C: Microorganisms multiply rapidly on metal surfaces without moisture
options.D: These surfaces act as common fomites for indirect contact spread

explanation: Exactly! High-touch areas easily collect germs from hands and pass them along to the next person, which is why cleaning them stops indirect spread.

question: Why must a patient rinse their mouth with water after using a steroid inhaler?

options.A: To wash away any bitter taste left behind on the tongue
options.B: To prevent the development of oral fungal infections like thrush
options.C: To stimulate saliva production for better lung absorption
options.D: To cool down the throat after the cold propellant spray

explanation: Steroids left behind in the mouth can lower local immunity and cause a fungal infection called thrush. A simple rinse and spit is all it takes to prevent this!

question: Why does the nurse gently help the patient tuck their chin and knees tight together during this procedure?

options.A: To keep the back muscles completely relaxed
options.B: To open up the spaces between the vertebrae
options.C: To slow down the heart rate during the tap
options.D: To prevent the patient from biting their tongue

explanation: Exactly! Flexing the spine widens the gaps, making it much easier for the doctor to insert the needle safely.

question: What does nutritional literacy refer to?

options.A: The knowledge of traditional recipes from different cultures
options.B: The talent for cooking meals without using any salt
options.C: The ability to understand and use basic nutrition information
options.D: The skill of growing vegetables in small indoor spaces

explanation: Nutritional literacy is about comprehending food labels and dietary advice to make healthy choices for the body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h4)

question: How do healthy endothelial cells help prevent abnormal blood clotting?

options.A: By triggering the intrinsic pathway during normal circulation
options.B: By releasing substances that actively inhibit platelet sticking
options.C: By producing large amounts of active thrombin into the blood
options.D: By slowing down the heart rate to reduce blood turbulence

explanation: Intact endothelium produces chemicals like prostacyclin and nitric oxide that discourage platelets from clumping together on normal vessel walls. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the most accurate way for parents to measure liquid paracetamol doses for children at home?

options.A: Using a standard kitchen teaspoon
options.B: Based on the child's height and shoe size
options.C: Using the age written on the medicine bottle
options.D: Based on the child's current body weight

explanation: Well done! Dosing by weight is the safest way to make sure the child gets the right amount, since kids of the same age can differ a lot in size.

question: Which of these checks is a key part of a neurovascular assessment on an injured arm or leg?

options.A: Total daily fluid intake and urine output
options.B: Bowel sound frequency and abdominal tone
options.C: Peripheral pulses and capillary refill
options.D: Client baseline blood cholesterol levels

explanation: Well done! Neurovascular checks are all about blood flow, feeling, and movement. Checking pulses and capillary refill tells us if blood is reaching the fingers and toes.

question: Why might a palliative patient feel severely short of breath even when their oxygen saturation is normal?

options.A: Pulse oximeters always give false readings in terminally ill patients
options.B: The patient is only pretending to panic to gain attention
options.C: Dyspnea is a subjective feeling influenced by many physical and emotional factors
options.D: Normal oxygen levels mean the lungs are working at full capacity

explanation: Breathlessness is a personal sensation that does not always match objective lab or monitor readings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h4)

question: Which drug is a commonly used over-the-counter motility inhibitor?

options.A: Salbutamol
options.B: Loperamide
options.C: Paracetamol
options.D: Omeprazole

explanation: Loperamide acts directly on intestinal opioid receptors to slow down bowel movements and is widely available for self-treatment. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h3)

question: How do daily tally sheets make your life easier during busy clinic shifts?

options.A: By providing quick tick marks that save time during monthly summaries
options.B: By automatically ordering new contraceptive drugs from the depot
options.C: By replacing the need to ever write in the client register
options.D: By diagnosing common side effects of hormonal contraceptives

explanation: Exactly! Tally sheets let you mark services as you go, saving you from a massive headache at the end of the month.

question: A patient has widespread body pain, tender points, and ongoing fatigue, but no visible joint swelling. What condition fits best?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Gout

explanation: Fibromyalgia is known for widespread pain and tender points, but unlike arthritis, it doesn't cause joint swelling or deformity. Great to keep this distinction in mind!

question: Which gender-related pressure often leads to higher rates of sexually transmitted infections among young males?

options.A: Strict adherence to solitary domestic lifestyles
options.B: Complete abstinence from all social gatherings
options.C: Fear of asking healthcare workers for vitamins
options.D: Pressure to prove masculinity through multiple partners

explanation: That's right! Societal pressure telling boys they must have multiple partners to 'prove' their manhood can unfortunately spread infections quickly.

question: What is the usual immediate effect of early marriage on a young girl's education?

options.A: It usually forces her to drop out of formal education completely
options.B: It gives her extra time to study advanced university subjects
options.C: It requires her to transfer to a special boarding school for married women
options.D: It has no measurable impact on her daily school attendance

explanation: Correct! Household chores and marital responsibilities almost always cut short a young girl's schooling.

question: What is the main physical problem for a patient with an obstructive lung disorder?

options.A: Inability of the chest wall to expand at all
options.B: Total absence of blood flow through the capillaries
options.C: Complete destruction of the pulmonary surfactant
options.D: Difficulty getting air out of the lungs quickly

explanation: Spot on! Obstructive diseases narrow or trap air inside the airways, making it really hard for patients to breathe air out fast. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h2)

question: How does long-term protein deficiency affect a patient who is trying to recover from an illness?

options.A: It delays wound healing and lowers immunity
options.B: It causes blood pressure to rise rapidly
options.C: It makes the bones overly dense and thick
options.D: It speeds up recovery from infections

explanation: Correct! Proteins are the building blocks your body uses to repair tissues and build immune cells. Without enough protein, healing takes much longer. You are mastering nutritional nursing!

question: What is the primary benefit of peer support groups for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Learning advanced medical surgical nursing procedures
options.B: Finding government-funded employment without interviews
options.C: Connecting with others who share similar experiences and offer practical advice
options.D: Receiving free prescription medications and medical supplies

explanation: Peer support reduces isolation and gives individuals hope by seeing others successfully navigate similar life challenges. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h6)

question: Besides checking physical lab results, what else should a nurse assess during routine consultations?

options.A: The patient's emotional readiness and coping style
options.B: The exact brand of clothing the patient prefers
options.C: The patient's long-term career and retirement plans
options.D: The architectural layout of the patient's house

explanation: Comprehensive nursing assessment evaluates mental health and emotional coping alongside physical health parameters. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why do medications absorb very slowly from the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: The epidermis blocks most medications from entering.
options.B: Sweat glands actively wash the medication away.
options.C: Skin cells in the dermis are tightly packed together.
options.D: The dermis has a very limited blood supply.

explanation: Limited blood vessels in the dermis mean the drug stays localized and is picked up very gradually by the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a symphysis joint in the body?

options.A: Pubic symphysis
options.B: Epiphyseal plate
options.C: Tooth socket
options.D: Skull suture

explanation: Awesome! The pubic symphysis is the classic textbook example where the right and left hip bones meet up front.

question: As a nurse caring for a yellow fever patient, which action is most critical to prioritize?

options.A: Administering routine oral iron supplements
options.B: Monitoring strict fluid intake and output
options.C: Encouraging high ambulation in the hallways
options.D: Applying cold water packs to the skin continuously

explanation: Brilliant! Because kidney failure can sneak up fast, tracking what goes in and out helps you catch trouble early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h5)

question: How is the bed arranged when a patient is placed in the Trendelenburg position?

options.A: Head is higher than the feet
options.B: Knees are bent and flat on the mattress
options.C: Head is lower than the feet
options.D: Bed is bent in the middle like a folding chair

explanation: In Trendelenburg, the whole bed tilts so the patient's head is lower than their feet. Gravity helps blood flow to the brain!

question: What major activity happens inside the brain during Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep?

options.A: The body completely shuts down all metabolic processes
options.B: Heart rate and breathing drop to their lowest daily levels
options.C: Intense brain activity and vivid dreaming occur
options.D: Muscles become completely rigid and unable to move

explanation: Even though your body is resting, your brain is super active during REM sleep! This is when we dream and process our emotions and memories.

question: Why do many advanced cancer patients experience severe weight loss and muscle wasting?

options.A: Permanent blockage of the large intestine only
options.B: A total loss of the brain's thirst center
options.C: Being forced to do too much heavy exercise
options.D: Metabolic changes caused by the tumor and treatments

explanation: Cancer changes how the body uses energy, leading to a condition called cachexia where muscle and fat break down fast. Nutritional support is so vital here.

question: What is the main benefit of using reflective listening during a patient interaction?

options.A: It allows the nurse to diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders
options.B: It speeds up the assessment process so the nurse can leave
options.C: It prevents the patient from expressing negative emotions
options.D: It confirms understanding and proves to the patient that they are heard

explanation: Reflecting back what a patient says assures them that you are actively listening and accurately grasping their feelings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the recommended compression rate per minute for performing adult CPR?

options.A: 80 to 100 compressions
options.B: 140 to 160 compressions
options.C: 60 to 80 compressions
options.D: 100 to 120 compressions

explanation: A rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute mimics an effective heart rate and maximizes blood flow. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the big advantage when a baby's head is fully flexed?

options.A: It stops the fetus from turning into a breech position
options.B: It presents a smaller head diameter to the birth canal
options.C: It speeds up the dilation of the external cervical os
options.D: It prevents early rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Well done! Tucking the chin means the baby leads with a smaller part of the head, making it much easier to pass through the pelvis.

question: Why might a patient experience a fast heartbeat (tachycardia) and hand tremors after using a rescue inhaler?

options.A: The inhaler device was shaken upside down before use
options.B: The patient drank cold water right before taking the medication
options.C: The medication has a systemic stimulant effect on beta receptors
options.D: The patient held their breath for too long during administration

explanation: Rescue inhalers often contain beta-agonists which, when absorbed into the bloodstream, stimulate the heart and nervous system. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is wound dehiscence?

options.A: The total numbness of nerves near the surgical site
options.B: The normal darkening of skin color around a healing cut
options.C: The rapid growth of new hair follicles over a scar
options.D: The partial or complete opening of a wound incision

explanation: Dehiscence happens when the edges of a healing wound separate and pull apart, requiring immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the main difference between problem-focused and emotion-focused coping?

options.A: Emotion-focused fixes physical organs, while problem-focused cures mental illness
options.B: Problem-focused is always unhealthy, while emotion-focused is always beneficial
options.C: Problem-focused involves denial, while emotion-focused involves physical exercise
options.D: Problem-focused deals with the actual stressor, while emotion-focused manages feelings about it

explanation: Problem-focused coping targets the root cause of stress, whereas emotion-focused coping helps soothe the emotional distress caused by the situation. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h3)

question: How does adding a little glucose to oral rehydration solution help the body absorb water?

options.A: Glucose creates a thick barrier that stops water from leaving the body
options.B: Glucose binds with sodium to pull water across the gut wall together
options.C: Glucose makes the drink taste sweet so the child will drink more
options.D: Glucose feeds the good bacteria so they can repair the damaged bowel

explanation: It's like a team effort! Sodium and glucose hitch a ride together on the same transport protein. As glucose is absorbed, it pulls sodium and water right along with it into the bloodstream.

question: What is the safest way to open the steam tent when the treatment is done?

options.A: Rip open the plastic tent quickly to let fresh air rush in
options.B: Leave the steam running while taking the patient out
options.C: Turn off the generator and open the canopy gradually
options.D: Wait until the room temperature drops below normal

explanation: Opening it slowly prevents a sudden blast of cool air from chilling your damp patient.

question: How does putting a heating pad on the lower belly help with post-abortion cramps?

options.A: It stops all vaginal bleeding instantly
options.B: It numbs the skin nerves permanently
options.C: It relaxes the uterine and pelvic muscles
options.D: It lowers the body temperature safely

explanation: Warmth boosts blood flow and helps tense muscles unwind, taking the sharp edge off those cramps. Simple and effective nursing comfort care!

question: What is pharmacovigilance?

options.A: The clinical trial phase testing drugs on healthy animal subjects
options.B: The mathematical calculation of correct pediatric drug dosages
options.C: The monitoring and prevention of adverse drug reactions
options.D: The process of manufacturing cheap generic pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Pharmacovigilance centers on detecting and tracking adverse drug events to ensure ongoing medication safety. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which family planning method gives you dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Intrauterine devices
options.D: Condoms

explanation: That's right! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block both sperm and infections, making them the only modern contraceptives that offer dual protection.

question: A nurse manager finds widespread failure in following a new infection control standard on the ward. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Investigate the root cause to see if supplies or training are lacking
options.B: Remove all handwashing stations from the clinical floor
options.C: Ignore the results because standards are rarely met anyway
options.D: Immediately suspend all nurses working on the morning shift

explanation: Good managers look for systemic reasons behind poor compliance, such as missing supplies or poor training, before blaming staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: During post-mortem care, why is a small pillow placed under the patient's head?

options.A: To prevent blood pooling and discoloration in the face
options.B: To make it easier to attach mechanical ventilators
options.C: To ensure the jaw stays wide open for viewing
options.D: To keep the patient comfortable during sleep cycles

explanation: Great job! Raising the head slightly stops gravity from pooling blood in the face, keeping a natural look.

question: What usually happens when a clinic doesn't have enough staff according to PHC standards?

options.A: Increased funding from international donor organizations
options.B: Faster turnaround times for routine laboratory investigations
options.C: Elimination of preventable communicable diseases
options.D: Staff burnout and reduced quality of care for patients

explanation: When too few hands carry a heavy load, nurses and staff get exhausted, and patients end up waiting longer or receiving rushed care.

question: Which of these actions is a major safety violation when storing medical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Locking the storage room door at night
options.B: Placing biohazard warning signs outside
options.C: Using a well-ventilated utility room
options.D: Leaving bags in public hospital corridors

explanation: Exactly right! Medical waste should never sit in public hallways where patients, visitors, or staff could trip over, knock over, or tear the bags.

question: How do volatile anesthetic gases typically leave the body during recovery from surgery?

options.A: Through the sweat glands on the skin
options.B: Through the kidneys into the urine
options.C: Through the lungs via exhalation
options.D: Through the liver into the bile

explanation: Gases and volatile liquids are breathed out through the respiratory tract without needing to be processed into urine first. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why do we ask patients to take off all jewelry and metallic objects before an X-ray?

options.A: They make the patient feel too heavy on the table
options.B: They attract stray electrical currents from the machine
options.C: They cause the X-ray tube to overheat quickly
options.D: They create dense white artifacts that hide details

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots that might hide important clues on the film.

question: What is a major advantage of using lower individual drug doses in synergistic therapy?

options.A: It completely removes the need for nursing blood monitoring
options.B: It reduces the risk of toxic side effects for the patient
options.C: It allows patients to stop taking the drugs much sooner
options.D: It ensures the medication works instantly without absorption

explanation: Because the drugs boost each other, we can use smaller doses to get the job done, keeping the patient safer from harsh side effects.

question: Why must long-term steroid therapy be gradually tapered off instead of stopped overnight?

options.A: It gives the adrenal glands time to wake up and make natural hormones again.
options.B: It gives the liver time to clear leftover chemicals.
options.C: It keeps the original disease from coming back instantly.
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling sudden weight loss and fatigue.

explanation: Brilliant! Long-term steroids put the body's natural hormone factories (adrenals) to sleep. Tapering slowly wakes them back up safely.

question: What is fluid balance in the human body?

options.A: Drinking the exact same amount of water every day
options.B: Water entering the body equals water leaving it
options.C: Having more electrolytes than water in the blood
options.D: Keeping all body water inside the blood vessels

explanation: Fluid balance simply means intake matches output over a given period to keep the system stable. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which heart condition is strongly linked to long-term chronic insomnia?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Pulmonary valve stenosis
options.C: Infective endocarditis
options.D: Congenital heart defect

explanation: When your body stays in a constant state of hyperarousal and misses out on restorative rest, your resting blood pressure creeps up, raising your risk for hypertension.

question: A clinic nurse tests a urine sample from a 32-week pregnant woman and finds protein in it. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Gestational hypertension with pre-eclampsia
options.B: Normal physiological kidney adaptation
options.C: Severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Dietary sugar overload from lunch

explanation: Protein in the urine combined with high blood pressure later in pregnancy is a classic warning sign of pre-eclampsia that needs immediate attention.

question: When doing a thoracentesis, where should the needle enter the chest to keep blood vessels and nerves safe?

options.A: Directly through the middle of the rib bone
options.B: Right beneath the bottom edge of the upper rib
options.C: Over the upper border of the lower rib
options.D: Through the soft center of the sternum bone

explanation: You're doing great! Nerves and blood vessels love to hide right under the bottom edge of each rib, so we slide the needle just over the top edge of the lower rib to avoid them.

question: Your patient keeps trying to talk and laugh with food in their mouth. What should you do?

options.A: Keep pushing the next spoonful of food into the mouth quickly
options.B: Scold the patient firmly for bad table manners
options.C: Ask the patient to finish chewing and swallowing before speaking
options.D: Remove the food tray immediately and skip the meal

explanation: Friendly reminders work best! Gently asking them to swallow first keeps them safe from choking while keeping the mood warm.

question: What is the main purpose of the Beers Criteria?

options.A: To identify medications that should be avoided in older adults
options.B: To determine the cheapest generic brand of heart medication
options.C: To calculate the exact dosage of antibiotics for kidney failure
options.D: To track how many pills a patient takes each day

explanation: The Beers Criteria is like a safety checklist for nurses and doctors, pointing out drugs that can be risky for older adults so we can protect them from harm.

question: What makes a female Guinea worm burst open and release her babies into water?

options.A: Exposure to sunlight
options.B: Ingestion of antibiotics
options.C: High fever in the host
options.D: Contact with cold water

explanation: Correct! When an infected person steps into a pond or well, the cool water signals the worm to release her larvae. You're mastering the transmission cycle!

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to help a patient with a poor appetite?

options.A: Offering small, frequent nutrient-dense snacks
options.B: Enhancing flavors with herbs and spices
options.C: Using adaptive eating devices like scooped plates
options.D: Forcing the patient to eat large meals quickly before they get tired

explanation: Rushing or forcing food only adds stress and wears the patient out, making them eat even less. Patience and gentle encouragement work best!

question: Why do you usually need two healthcare workers to measure the length of a baby?

options.A: One person writes down the numbers while the other watches the monitor
options.B: One holds the head steady while the other straightens the legs and moves the footboard
options.C: Infants are too heavy for a single nurse to lift onto the measuring table
options.D: Hospital policy strictly forbids any nurse from working alone with babies

explanation: Babies wiggle a lot! Having one person hold the head safely while the second person gently straightens the legs gets you an accurate measurement.

question: Which laboratory test results should a nurse check first to see how well a patient's kidneys are clearing drugs?

options.A: White blood cell count and platelets
options.B: Liver enzymes and serum albumin
options.C: Serum creatinine and BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen)
options.D: Sodium and potassium electrolytes

explanation: Serum creatinine and BUN are your go-to lab values in the ward for checking how well the kidneys are filtering waste and clearing out medications.

question: What is the main root cause behind gender-based violence?

options.A: Genetics and hereditary health disorders
options.B: Temporary financial stress in families
options.C: Lack of formal education in victims
options.D: Unequal power dynamics between genders

explanation: Spot on! Gender-based violence usually stems from imbalances of power between men and women in society, rather than just money troubles or genetics.

question: What is the main reason to check in on the psychological needs of a dying patient's family?

options.A: To identify burnout and connect them with support resources
options.B: To force them to leave the hospital room to rest
options.C: To diagnose them with a formal psychiatric illness
options.D: To judge whether they love the patient enough

explanation: Family members can easily exhaust themselves. Checking in helps us spot caregiver burnout early and offer them the support they need.

question: Which combination of vital sign changes makes up Cushing's triad (a sign of high pressure inside the brain)?

options.A: Hypertension, tachypnea, high fever
options.B: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, shallow respirations
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, rapid breathing

explanation: Cushing's triad is a critical warning sign! Watch for high blood pressure with a wide gap between top and bottom numbers, a very slow pulse, and weird breathing.

question: A patient gets too full during meals and leaves food untouched. What strategy should the nurse suggest?

options.A: Drink two large glasses of water immediately before eating
options.B: Wait until evening and consume the entire day's food at once
options.C: Eat small, frequent meals and snacks throughout the day
options.D: Stop eating all solid foods and rely strictly on clear broths

explanation: Grazing on smaller, nutrient-dense meals every few hours prevents early fullness and helps patients hit their daily calorie goals easily. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h6)

question: Why are the tiny blood vessels (capillaries) inside endocrine glands specially built?

options.A: They lack endothelial linings to let whole secretory cells escape
options.B: They have thick walls to withstand high pressure from hormone surges
options.C: They are fenestrated to allow quick entry of hormones into the bloodstream
options.D: They contain valves that prevent the backflow of endocrine secretions

explanation: Fenestrated just means 'having tiny windows or pores'! These little pores make the capillary walls super leaky in a good way, helping hormones hop straight into your blood in no time.

question: Why is the nurse's voice so important in a collaborative healthcare team?

options.A: Nurses hold sole legal authority over all hospital budget allocations
options.B: Nurses are the only professionals trained to diagnose chronic illnesses
options.C: Nurses dictate the operational hours of every hospital department
options.D: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside observing patients

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses are right there at the bedside day and night, they spot subtle changes in patients before anyone else does.

question: Why do we have to be extra careful when disposing of cytotoxic (chemotherapy) drugs?

options.A: Expired tablets turn into sweet-tasting candy that attracts children
options.B: These drugs instantly catch fire when exposed to ordinary air
options.C: Cytotoxic drugs are designed to destroy cells and can damage healthy tissue and genetic material
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs make the local soil extremely fertile for crops

explanation: Spot on! These medications are specially made to kill fast-growing cells, meaning they can harm healthy human tissue and our environment if carelessly thrown out.

question: Why is an injury high up on the spinal cord considered a major medical emergency?

options.A: It stops the digestive system from absorbing water
options.B: It automatically causes complete memory loss
options.C: It can paralyze the muscles needed for breathing
options.D: It prevents the heart from producing blood cells

explanation: That's right! High cervical injuries cut off nerve signals to the diaphragm and chest, making it hard or impossible for the patient to breathe on their own without quick support.

question: A patient needs a nasogastric tube but has a history of a severe skull fracture at the base of the head. What should you do?

options.A: Perform the insertion quickly while the patient is asleep
options.B: Proceed with normal insertion using extra lubrication
options.C: Consult the doctor because putting a tube through the nose is risky here
options.D: Insert the tube through the mouth instead without checking

explanation: A basilar skull fracture means the bone near the brain is damaged, so passing a tube through the nose could accidentally enter the brain. Always check with your senior or doctor!

question: Why do nurses make mitered corners when tucking in hospital bed sheets?

options.A: To create a neat, secure fit that prevents sheets from pulling loose
options.B: To allow air to circulate freely around the patient's feet
options.C: To make it easier to fold the mattress in half for storage
options.D: To comply with international hotel standards for hospital rooms

explanation: Correct! Mitered corners lock the bedding tightly in place, meaning restless patient movement won't easily pull the sheets untucked.

question: Why must you remove a medication patch from a patient's chest before putting on AED pads?

options.A: The medication will instantly enter the machine and break the processor.
options.B: The patch makes the skin too slippery for the rescuer to press hard.
options.C: The patch will absorb the conductive gel and ruin the AED pads.
options.D: The patch can block the electrical current and cause skin burns.

explanation: Medication patches can interfere with the electricity and even cause nasty skin burns. Always peel them off and wipe the skin clean first!

question: Globally, where does the highest burden of unsafe medical care usually happen?

options.A: Rural community pharmacies in wealthy nations
options.B: Private specialized clinics in Europe
options.C: Advanced research hospitals in North America
options.D: Low- and middle-income countries

explanation: Resource-limited settings face tough system challenges that unfortunately lead to higher rates of preventable harm.

question: Which main hormone does the body release during prolonged stress to keep your energy up?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Cortisol is often called the stress hormone. When stress sticks around for a while, cortisol steps in to keep your energy levels steady. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h2)

question: How do cross-sectional study findings help Nigerian nurse managers in clinical practice?

options.A: By proving which nurse caused specific patient readmissions
options.B: By eliminating the need for daily nursing shift handovers
options.C: By guaranteeing permanent funding from international donor agencies
options.D: By providing local data to improve resource allocation and healthcare planning

explanation: Local data helps managers see real community needs clearly, making it easier to send staff and supplies right where they are needed most.

question: Why are fresh flowers and live plants banned from the room of an immunocompromised patient?

options.A: They attract stinging insects into the hospital room
options.B: Their soil and standing water harbor dangerous fungi
options.C: Their strong scent can trigger severe allergic asthma
options.D: They consume too much oxygen in a closed space

explanation: Soil and stagnant water are breeding grounds for fungi and bacteria that can easily cause severe infections in patients with low white blood cells. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h3)

question: How do transdermal patches differ from ordinary skin creams?

options.A: Transdermal patches are applied exclusively to mucous membranes
options.B: Patches only treat localized surface skin infections
options.C: Transdermal patches are designed for systemic absorption
options.D: Standard creams always enter the bloodstream faster than patches

explanation: While regular creams usually stay local, patches slowly deliver medicine through the skin and into the bloodstream to treat the entire body. Brilliant thinking!

question: What do we call an actual bruise of the brain tissue that comes with bleeding?

options.A: Contusion
options.B: Hematoma
options.C: Concussion
options.D: Transection

explanation: Spot on! A brain contusion is essentially a bruise on the brain itself. A concussion is different because it usually doesn't show physical tearing or structural damage on scans.

question: What makes adaptive immunity so special compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical barriers like unbroken skin layers
options.B: It responds instantly within the first few minutes of exposure
options.C: It creates specific immunological memory against specific pathogens
options.D: It requires no cellular coordination or chemical signaling

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive immunity never forgets. Once it fights a germ, it remembers it, so if that same germ attacks later, your body fights back much faster and stronger.

question: Why are pregnant women advised to drink fluids between meals rather than during meals?

options.A: To keep stomach acid completely inactive during digestion
options.B: To prevent over-stretching the stomach which can trigger vomiting
options.C: To ensure the body absorbs all the vitamins from the solid food
options.D: To stop the kidneys from working too hard after eating

explanation: Filling the stomach with both food and large amounts of liquid at the same time increases pressure and promotes vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when caring for an acute poisoning patient?

options.A: Drawing blood samples for comprehensive toxicology screens
options.B: Administering activated charcoal to clear the stomach
options.C: Securing the airway, breathing, and circulation
options.D: Finding out the exact name of the ingested chemical

explanation: Always remember your ABCs! Keeping the patient breathing and stable comes way before finding out what they swallowed.

question: What is the purpose of the safety limits (guardrails) on smart infusion pumps?

options.A: To automatically calculate patient drug dosages without nurse input
options.B: To track how many supplies are used during each shift
options.C: To lock the pump door so patients cannot change settings
options.D: To warn nurses if a programmed dose is outside safe limits

explanation: Exactly! Guardrails act like a helpful safety net, popping up a warning if a number looks too high or too low.

question: Why is it a big no-no to use petroleum jelly or body lotion with a latex condom?

options.A: Petroleum products freeze the latex and crack it
options.B: Oils trap bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.C: Oil-based products break down and weaken latex
options.D: Lotions make the condom slide off too easily

explanation: Correct! Oils make latex dissolve and tear easily, completely ruining its protective power. Always stick to water-based lubricants!

question: An experienced nurse is bored with routine duties and wants to take on hospital quality projects. What management approach fits best?

options.A: Reducing the nurse's daily patient assignment size
options.B: Focusing strictly on increasing the base hourly salary
options.C: Threatening disciplinary action for minor paperwork delays
options.D: Providing opportunities for professional achievement and growth

explanation: You nailed it! When a nurse is looking for a challenge, giving them room to grow and achieve is the best way to keep them inspired.

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and increased muscle weakness
options.B: Enhanced immune system function
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic stroke symptoms
options.D: Rapid muscle growth and increased strength

explanation: Brilliant! Without good food and protein, the body simply doesn't have the fuel to repair tissues or build strength.

question: What is the primary goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: Empowering local communities to support and integrate children with disabilities
options.B: Eliminating the need for any hospital visits
options.C: Training only foreign doctors in local customs
options.D: Relocating all special children to central urban orphanages

explanation: CBR is all about using local resources and community spirit to ensure children with disabilities thrive right where they live.

question: When should hand hygiene be performed during a physical examination?

options.A: At the end of the entire shift
options.B: Only when the patient has a known infection
options.C: Before and after touching the patient
options.D: Only if the nurse's hands look visibly dirty

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective way to stop the spread of germs between patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a well-known example of a steroid hormone?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Cortisol is our classic stress steroid hormone, made by the adrenal cortex straight from cholesterol. You'll hear about cortisol constantly in medical-surgical nursing!

question: What is the most common local side effect of a topical skin medication?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure
options.B: Contact dermatitis and redness at the site
options.C: Complete hair loss on the scalp
options.D: Severe high blood pressure

explanation: Mild skin irritation, redness, or itching right where the cream was applied are the most common reactions to topical products.

question: Why do doctors often choose laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: It guarantees zero risk of post-operative complications
options.B: It causes less pain and allows a faster recovery
options.C: It requires no special surgical equipment or training
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for general anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Because the cuts (incisions) are very small, there is less damage to the body, less pain afterwards, and the patient gets back on their feet much quicker.

question: What is the main job of Regulatory T-cells (T-regs)?

options.A: To engulf large cellular debris via phagocytosis in tissues
options.B: To suppress excessive immune responses and prevent autoimmunity
options.C: To form physical barriers on mucosal and skin surfaces
options.D: To produce high affinity antibodies against foreign bacteria

explanation: Well done! T-regs act like peacekeepers, calming down the immune system after a fight so it doesn't accidentally attack healthy body tissue.

question: Which finding during a routine IV assessment suggests the dressing needs immediate replacement?

options.A: The intravenous fluid bag is half full of normal saline
options.B: The patient reports sleeping well through the entire night
options.C: The dressing edges are lifting and exposing the insertion site
options.D: The extension tubing is coiled neatly on the bed sheet

explanation: Lifting dressings lose their sterile seal, increasing the risk of bacteria entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is it so important to report a disease outbreak quickly in your community?

options.A: It guarantees free medical treatment for all citizens
options.B: It stops patients from visiting traditional healers
options.C: It helps health agencies spot unusual disease patterns early
options.D: It reduces the cost of prescription drugs in pharmacies

explanation: Spotting cases early gives health teams the heads-up they need to track trends and stop epidemics in their tracks. You're building solid public health sense!

question: Where is the best spot on the finger to prick for a blood sample?

options.A: The direct center of the finger pad
options.B: The base of the fingernail bed
options.C: The soft skin right over the joint
options.D: The side of the fingertip

explanation: The sides of our fingertips have fewer nerve endings than the pads, making the prick much less painful for your patient.

question: Why is a nutrition history considered a vital part of a standard patient admission assessment?

options.A: It helps catch early warning signs of poor nourishment before severe illness develops
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical examination findings
options.C: It ensures the hospital kitchen meets local food safety inspection standards
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never experience any weight loss

explanation: Early identification of dietary issues allows nurses to intervene before nutritional problems turn into major health complications. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h1)

question: Why do nurses prefer IV medications over oral tablets during severe emergencies?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It delivers medication directly into the bloodstream for fast action
options.C: Oral medications are illegal in hospital emergency units
options.D: It eliminates the need for any dosage calculations

explanation: IV meds skip the digestive system completely, hitting the bloodstream instantly when every single second counts.

question: A patient is being discharged after treatment for pelvic inflammatory disease. What key advice should you give her?

options.A: Finish all your prescribed antibiotics even if you feel better.
options.B: Stop all physical activities permanently.
options.C: Avoid drinking water for two days.
options.D: Expect severe pelvic pain for three months.

explanation: Never let them stop early! Remind patients that feeling better doesn't mean the germs are gone. Finishing the dose stops the infection from bouncing back stronger.

question: Why do many women in Nigeria still resort to unsafe abortions despite strict laws?

options.A: Abortion being completely free in government hospitals
options.B: Desire to experience traditional surgical practices
options.C: Lack of access to safe services and modern contraceptives
options.D: Legal encouragement from local community leaders

explanation: Spot on! When family planning services and safe care are hard to reach, vulnerable women sadly turn to dangerous alternatives.

question: How is a dilator different from a regular feeding tube?

options.A: A dilator is specifically designed to stretch tight strictures.
options.B: A dilator is only used for temporary fluid drainage.
options.C: A feeding tube contains a built-in cutting blade.
options.D: A feeding tube is rigid while dilators are always soft.

explanation: While feeding tubes are for giving food, dilators are specially sized and shaped to gently stretch out narrowed tubes in the body.

question: A community health nurse checks the weekly antenatal clinic register every Friday to ensure attendance numbers are steady. What type of activity is this?

options.A: Monitoring
options.B: Resource mobilization
options.C: Needs assessment
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Reviewing registers weekly during the project to track progress is ongoing monitoring. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: How does showing respect for a family's household customs help your patient care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change household rules permanently
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of medical supplies
options.C: It builds trust and encourages the family to cooperate with the care plan
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never experience complications

explanation: Brilliant! When people feel respected in their own homes, they trust you more—and a trusting patient is much more likely to follow your health advice.

question: What is an endemic disease?

options.A: A rare disease that only appears once every century
options.B: A physical injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident
options.C: A medical condition caused entirely by eating too much sugar
options.D: An infection that is constantly present within a specific region

explanation: Endemic diseases, such as malaria in tropical climates, maintain a steady presence in the local area. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: What type of vaginal discharge would a nurse expect to see in a patient with acute postpartum endometritis?

options.A: Dry with no fluid present
options.B: Foul-smelling and purulent
options.C: Clear, watery, and odorless
options.D: Thick, white, and cottage-cheese-like

explanation: When bacteria party inside the closed womb, they produce pus (purulent discharge) that often carries a very unpleasant, foul smell.

question: Why do fallopian tube defects often happen alongside kidney issues in an unborn baby?

options.A: The fallopian tubes secrete fluids that nourish the developing kidneys
options.B: The urinary and reproductive systems develop close together in the embryo
options.C: Both organs share the exact same blood supply during adult life
options.D: The kidneys filter hormones that control the growth of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Makes sense, right? Because kidneys and reproductive organs grow side-by-side in the embryo, a developmental hiccup often affects both.

question: A nurse is talking to an overweight teenager about healthy eating. What is the most encouraging and effective approach?

options.A: Directly warning the teenager about how bad their body shape looks
options.B: Focusing the discussion on energy, athletic performance, and well-being without shaming
options.C: Ignoring diet completely and focusing only on prescription medication
options.D: Strictly forbidding all favorite foods to force rapid weight loss

explanation: Encouragement wins every time! Focusing on feeling good, having more energy, and performing well works much better than shaming or strict starvation diets.

question: What is the first priority when assessing and managing a patient presenting with acute shock?

options.A: Ensuring a patent airway and supporting breathing
options.B: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
options.C: Drawing blood for full laboratory investigations
options.D: Explaining the hospital bill to the relatives

explanation: Regardless of the setting, the ABCDE protocol mandates that airway and breathing take precedence in any resuscitation emergency. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h8)

question: When a patient is prescribed both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, which one should they generally use first?

options.A: Whichever medication is closer to hand
options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why are geriatric syndromes described as having multiple causes?

options.A: They result from impairments across multiple body systems
options.B: They are exclusively caused by psychological stress
options.C: They are caused by a single specific bacterial pathogen
options.D: They only occur in patients with genetic mutations

explanation: Geriatric syndromes (like falls or confusion) usually happen when little things go wrong across different parts of the body all at once, rather than just one single disease.

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during active labor?

options.A: To record financial payments made by the patient at the hospital
options.B: To calculate the exact date of conception for the mother
options.C: To track labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.D: To determine the blood group and genotype of the newborn

explanation: The partograph is your trusty graphical roadmap of labor. It helps you spot when things are taking too long so you can act fast.

question: What is the best way to handle a young child who refuses to eat a newly introduced vegetable?

options.A: Offer it repeatedly over time alongside familiar foods without forcing them
options.B: Punish the child by sending them away from the dinner table immediately
options.C: Stop offering all vegetables permanently to avoid any further stress
options.D: Force the child to finish every single bite on the plate before sleeping

explanation: Children often need multiple exposures to a new food before accepting it, and pressure only increases mealtime anxiety. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h6)

question: Which nutritional deficiency is most common in adolescent girls who have heavy periods and poor diets?

options.A: Beriberi and Thiamine deficiency
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Scurvy and Vitamin C deficiency
options.D: Rickets and Vitamin D deficiency

explanation: Monthly blood loss plus meals lacking in iron easily leads to anemia. It's why adolescent girls often look pale or feel constantly tired, and why nutritional education is so crucial!

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when starting community mobilisation?

options.A: Entry and sensitization with local leaders
options.B: Building a brand new brick health clinic
options.C: Punishing people who miss immunization days
options.D: Writing the final project evaluation report

explanation: You must enter respectfully and introduce yourself to leaders before trying to assess needs or plan actions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: Before you start collecting data for a community diagnosis, what is usually the very first step?

options.A: Securing administrative clearance and mobilizing stakeholders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry
options.D: Treating all sick children with antibiotics

explanation: You always want to respect local authority! Getting permission and greeting community leaders comes first before marching in with clipboards.

question: Why is training in adolescent psychology helpful for clinical nurses?

options.A: It helps nurses understand the unique developmental and communication needs of teenagers
options.B: It allows nurses to prescribe adult psychiatric medications without a doctor
options.C: It legally forces teenagers to follow every medical instruction given
options.D: It replaces the need for basic nursing assessment skills in emergencies

explanation: Specialized training helps you talk with teens on their level, handling sensitive topics with patience and care.

question: What is the main difference between vaccine efficacy and vaccine effectiveness?

options.A: Effectiveness applies only to viral vaccines while efficacy applies to bacterial vaccines
options.B: Effectiveness is determined in a laboratory before animal testing begins
options.C: Efficacy measures performance in ideal trials while effectiveness measures performance in everyday settings
options.D: Efficacy is measured in children while effectiveness is measured in adults

explanation: Think of efficacy as how a vaccine performs in a controlled lab test, while effectiveness is how it holds up for real people out in the community! You've got this.

question: A patient develops a sudden, severe facial swelling and rash immediately after starting a new antibiotic. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Reassure the patient that rashes are normal and tell them to finish the drug
options.B: Double the fluid intake and ask the patient to sleep off the swelling
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled outpatient clinic visit to mention the rash
options.D: Stop the drug immediately, notify the prescriber, and submit an adverse reaction report

explanation: Signs of a severe allergic reaction require immediate cessation of the offending drug, medical notification, and formal reporting. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is a direct cost for a patient admitted to the surgical ward?

options.A: The general lighting bill for the hospital parking lot
options.B: The monthly salary of the hospital accountant
options.C: The specific surgical gloves worn during their operation
options.D: The cost of repairing the main hospital elevator

explanation: Because those gloves were used directly for that single patient's surgery, they count as a direct cost. Makes total sense when you picture it in the theater!

question: What should a nurse do if a sterile instrument pack has a torn or damp wrapper?

options.A: Discard or return the item because sterility is lost
options.B: Wipe the outside with alcohol and place it back on the shelf
options.C: Use it quickly before any dust can settle inside
options.D: Ask another nurse to approve using it for a minor dressing

explanation: Any damage or moisture to a sterile wrapper compromises the barrier, meaning the instruments are no longer safe to use. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Which organs take the biggest hit from long-term iron overload caused by frequent blood transfusions?

options.A: Lungs, pleura, and upper airways
options.B: Brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves
options.C: Liver, heart, and endocrine glands
options.D: Stomach, intestines, and pancreas

explanation: Extra iron loves to settle down in hard-working organs like the liver, the heart muscle, and hormone-making glands, eventually causing tissue damage if not treated.

question: What is the main reason nurses wash out (irrigate) a newborn's infected eyes with sterile saline?

options.A: To kill drug-resistant bacteria instantly
options.B: To stimulate tear duct development
options.C: To remove accumulated purulent discharge
options.D: To numb the surface of the cornea

explanation: Exactly! Clearing away all that pus helps the prescribed eye meds actually reach the skin and tissues where they need to work.

question: How is general hospital waste different from infectious waste?

options.A: Infectious waste is always heavier than general waste boxes
options.B: General waste requires special incineration before leaving the ward
options.C: General waste is non-hazardous and similar to normal household trash
options.D: Infectious waste comes only from the hospital kitchen

explanation: Exactly! General waste has no contamination risk (like empty paper packaging), unlike infectious items that carry pathogens.

question: What is the main purpose of following clinical protocols in nursing practice?

options.A: To ensure patients receive a consistent, high standard of care
options.B: To reduce the salary budget for nursing administrators
options.C: To increase the speed of routine paperwork completion
options.D: To eliminate the need for critical thinking during emergencies

explanation: Protocols provide a reliable roadmap based on best evidence, ensuring safe and consistent treatment across all shifts and staff. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h4)

question: If a community shows both a high Maternal Mortality Ratio and a high Total Fertility Rate, what is the most likely link?

options.A: Contraceptive methods are causing direct medical toxicity
options.B: Frequent pregnancies without adequate spacing strain maternal health
options.C: Women are choosing surgical sterilization too early in life
options.D: Hospital records are systematically miscalculated by local staff

explanation: When pregnancies happen back-to-back without enough resting time, a mother's body gets worn out, which sadly drives up complication and mortality rates.

question: Why is continuous electronic fetal monitoring so important during preterm labour?

options.A: Preterm fetuses tolerate the stress of contractions poorly
options.B: It stops the progress of cervical dilation automatically
options.C: It is the only way to calculate the exact due date
options.D: It prevents the mother from experiencing any back pain

explanation: Preterm babies have delicate reserves, so watching the monitor closely helps us catch signs of distress early. You're learning top-tier patient safety!

question: Why are phytochemicals from plants not officially classed as 'essential nutrients' even though they are great for our health?

options.A: They are entirely artificial compounds created during food processing
options.B: The body does not suffer an immediate deficiency syndrome if they are absent
options.C: They only exist in animal tissues rather than plant-based foods
options.D: They provide too many calories for daily metabolic requirements

explanation: Spot on! Missing essential nutrients causes specific deficiency diseases, whereas missing phytochemicals just means you miss out on extra health boosts.

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of knowing research classifications for a nurse?

options.A: Selecting safe treatments backed by strong studies
options.B: Understanding professional nursing journals easily
options.C: Designing simple nursing projects during training
options.D: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently

explanation: Spot on! Nurses don't diagnose complex conditions independently just by looking at research types—diagnosis takes formal clinical training and specific professional scope. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the biggest danger of running a nursing study with a sample size that is way too small?

options.A: Making the data analysis so complex that computers take days to run it
options.B: Failing to get approval from the hospital ethics and research board
options.C: Missing a real treatment effect or clinical difference due to lack of power
options.D: Incurring massive financial debt from buying unnecessary hospital supplies

explanation: Exactly! Small samples are too weak to show the truth, often tricking researchers into thinking a great intervention didn't work when it actually did.

question: A new mother on her third day postpartum says her breasts are hard, warm, and very painful. What is likely going on?

options.A: A blocked lactiferous duct due to tight clothing
options.B: Physiological engorgement as milk production begins in large volumes
options.C: Acute mastitis caused by a bacterial infection from the infant's mouth
options.D: Absence of oxytocin release during feedings

explanation: This is standard postpartum breast engorgement! The sudden rush of milk, blood, and fluids can make the breasts feel very full and tender around day three.

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body make a lot more blood?

options.A: To lower her core body temperature
options.B: To make up for heavy monthly bleeding
options.C: To prevent swollen veins in her legs
options.D: To supply the growing placenta and baby

explanation: A pregnant body increases its blood volume to make sure the placenta and the growing baby get all the oxygen and nutrients they need.

question: Which of these is a key part of active listening for a nurse leader?

options.A: Listening to understand concerns rather than just waiting to speak
options.B: Writing down every single word spoken without making eye contact
options.C: Interrupting the speaker frequently to correct minor grammar mistakes
options.D: Agreeing with every demand made by patients and staff members

explanation: Active listening means turning off your mental reply-generator and genuinely trying to see things from the other person's point of view.

question: Before puberty starts, what does the central nervous system usually do regarding reproductive hormones?

options.A: It produces excess adult levels
options.B: It completely shuts down the pituitary
options.C: It suppresses hormone release
options.D: It secretes erratic daily spikes

explanation: You got it! Throughout childhood, the brain actively keeps reproductive hormone levels low and quiet until the body is mature enough for puberty.

question: Which ethical principle gives a competent patient the right to refuse a prescribed medication?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy is all about respecting the patient's right to make independent choices about their own body and healthcare journey.

question: What is the main focus when managing non-communicable diseases in clinical practice?

options.A: Isolating the patient in a specialized ward to prevent spreading
options.B: Achieving a complete cure within a fourteen-day treatment window
options.C: Administering a short course of antibiotics to kill the pathogen
options.D: Long-term symptom control and prevention of complications

explanation: Correct! Because chronic conditions last a lifetime, our care focuses on keeping symptoms under control, protecting organs, and helping patients live well.

question: Why do midwives and doctors check red blood cell indices (like MCV) in an anemic pregnant woman?

options.A: To determine the specific structural classification and underlying cause of the anaemia
options.B: To check if the mother has developed gestational diabetes
options.C: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus
options.D: To calculate the precise delivery date based on red cell lifespan

explanation: Brilliant! MCV tells you the size of the red blood cells. Are they too small (microcytic), too big (macrocytic), or normal? That helps you know if it's iron trouble, folate trouble, or something else.

question: Why are the bones of the fetal skull separated by sutures and fontanelles during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent the cerebrospinal fluid from building up inside the cranial cavity
options.B: To allow the skull bones to overlap and change shape inside the pelvis
options.C: To protect the baby's brain from normal changes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: To provide extra room for rapid brain growth during the first stage of labour

explanation: The gaps in the skull allow the bones to shift and overlap, reducing the head's diameter so it can pass safely through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: What is the main goal of using a clean delivery kit during a home birth?

options.A: To speed up the progress of the first stage of labor
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing by the birth attendant
options.C: To prevent infection for both mother and newborn
options.D: To provide entertainment for the family during labor

explanation: Simple and crucial—the kit provides clean, germ-free items to stop harmful bacteria from causing infections during and after birth.

question: What is a potential long-term complication for an infant who survives a severe intracranial hemorrhage?

options.A: Developmental delays and seizure disorders
options.B: Early closure of all body joints
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of smell only
options.D: Enlargement of the hands and feet

explanation: Significant bleeding inside the cranium can damage brain tissue, leading to chronic neurological issues like seizures and delayed milestones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h6)

question: Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB) means the bacteria are resistant to which two key drugs?

options.A: Isoniazid and Rifampicin
options.B: Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
options.C: Streptomycin and Amikacin
options.D: Levofloxacin and Bedaquiline

explanation: MDR-TB specifically means the two heavy-hitters of first-line treatment—isoniazid and rifampicin—no longer work against the strain.

question: How can community health nurses help lower the number of unsafe abortions?

options.A: By dispelling contraceptive myths and promoting youth-friendly reproductive health services
options.B: By teaching women how to safely use herbal concoctions at home
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal abortions in local villages
options.D: By distributing heavy surgical instruments to traditional birth attendants

explanation: Education and open access to family planning stop unwanted pregnancies before they happen—that is the most powerful prevention!

question: What does PMTCT stand for in maternal and child health nursing?

options.A: Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission
options.B: Primary Medical Treatment and Care Techniques
options.C: Pediatric Medication Testing and Clinical Trials
options.D: Post-Natal Maternal Complication Treatment

explanation: PMTCT stands for Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission, which encompasses strategies to stop vertical HIV spread during pregnancy, birth, and breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is keeping our gut healthy so important for our overall wellbeing?

options.A: It prevents all forms of cardiovascular disease instantly
options.B: A large part of the immune system lives in the gut
options.C: It controls voluntary muscle movement in the limbs
options.D: The gut produces red blood cells for circulation

explanation: You got it! A huge chunk of our immune defense actually lives right inside our intestines, which is why a happy gut keeps the whole body strong.

question: Why is family planning counseling considered such an important part of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: It cures underlying pelvic inflammatory disease without antibiotics
options.B: It stops all immediate bleeding from uterine perforation
options.C: It helps women prevent another unwanted pregnancy in the near future
options.D: It is required by law to permanently sterilize every female patient

explanation: Spot on! Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion, so giving timely contraceptive advice helps prevent repeat unsafe procedures.

question: Which of these is a great environmental change to help a patient with low vision stay safe?

options.A: Using high-contrast colors on stairs and doorway edges
options.B: Placing scattered small rugs across hard floors for comfort
options.C: Keeping furniture rearranged frequently to test spatial memory
options.D: Dimming all indoor lights to prevent harsh eye strain

explanation: High contrast is a lifesaver! Marking steps and door edges clearly helps patients with low vision see boundaries easily and prevents nasty falls.

question: How does negative feedback differ from positive feedback?

options.A: Negative feedback speeds up heart rate, while positive feedback slows it down
options.B: Negative feedback only works in the brain, while positive feedback works in the skin
options.C: Negative feedback causes disease, while positive feedback cures it
options.D: Negative feedback reverses a change, while positive feedback amplifies it

explanation: Don't let the names fool you! Negative feedback works to bring levels back down to normal (like cooling down when you're hot), while positive feedback pushes a change further until a task is done (like during childbirth).

question: A patient has a cough that gets worse during workdays but clears up completely on weekends. What should you suspect?

options.A: An acute infection caught during weekend travel
options.B: A symptom unrelated to lifestyle or environment
options.C: An occupational exposure in the work environment
options.D: A purely genetic heart condition
