explanation: When symptoms flare up only during work hours and ease during rest days, it's a huge clue that something at work is causing it.

question: Which drug class works by acting as faulty building blocks that trick the reverse transcriptase enzyme?

options.A: Integrase Inhibitors
options.B: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs)
options.C: Entry Inhibitors
options.D: Protease Inhibitors (PIs)

explanation: Well done! NRTIs send in fake building blocks. The virus gets tricked into using them, which completely halts the creation of its viral DNA.

question: A rural community suffers from a high rate of waterborne diseases like cholera. Besides treating sick patients, which action represents true intersectoral collaboration?

options.A: Asking nurses to work overtime shifts in the treatment tent
options.B: Increasing the price of local river water to discourage drinking it
options.C: Ordering more intravenous fluids from the central medical store
options.D: Partnering with public works and local leaders to build safe boreholes

explanation: Working with public works engineers addresses the environmental source of the problem rather than just treating the resulting illness. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: A 14-year-old boy shows no physical signs of testicular enlargement or puberty yet. How would a nurse document this finding?

options.A: Precocious puberty
options.B: Normal variant
options.C: Delayed puberty
options.D: Acquired gigantism

explanation: You got it! When physical maturation hasn't started by age 14 in males, it is clinically categorized as delayed puberty.

question: What does 'endocrine resistance' mean in cancer treatment?

options.A: When the liver breaks down medication too slowly to be effective
options.B: When the endocrine glands stop producing hormones permanently
options.C: When the patient's immune system attacks all circulating hormone pills
options.D: When tumor cells stop responding to a drug that once blocked their receptors

explanation: It's like cancer cells finding a loophole; even though the medication is blocking their usual path, the cancer figures out a way around it and keeps growing. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is a major public health downside of relying solely on harsh criminal punishment for substance abuse?

options.A: It automatically cures physical dependence within forty-eight hours
options.B: It forces pharmaceutical companies to stop manufacturing all antibiotics
options.C: It drives vulnerable drug users underground and prevents them from seeking medical help
options.D: It eliminates every single illegal drug farm in the entire world

explanation: When people fear police arrest and prison, they tend to stay away from hospitals during overdoses or medical crises, which puts lives at risk.

question: Why are bedside nurses considered the main line of defense against hospital complications?

options.A: They perform all diagnostic lab tests
options.B: They prescribe the preventative medications
options.C: They discharge patients independently
options.D: They spend the most time observing the patient

explanation: Spot on! Because you are right there at the bedside day in and day out, you notice those tiny, early changes long before anyone else does.

question: Six hours after a circumcision, you notice steady, active bleeding from the wound edge. What is your FIRST nursing action?

options.A: Soak the entire genital area in warm soapy bath water
options.B: Apply direct, firm pressure to the bleeding site with sterile gauze
options.C: Administer a stat dose of intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.D: Wait patiently to see if the bleeding stops on its own within an hour

explanation: Always start with direct pressure using sterile gauze to control bleeding while you call for the doctor to assist.

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for preparing the lining of the womb for implantation?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Well done! Progesterone takes the lead in the second half of the cycle, making the womb lining thick and cozy for a potential pregnancy.

question: When cancer treatment cannot cure the disease, but aims to stop tumor growth and extend life, what is this main goal called?

options.A: Palliation
options.B: Cure
options.C: Prevention
options.D: Control

explanation: You've got this! When complete cure isn't possible, 'control' is the goal—stopping the cancer from spreading further to help the patient live a longer, fuller life.

question: What part of the communication loop lets the nurse know if the client understood the message?

options.A: Sender
options.B: Channel
options.C: Interference
options.D: Feedback

explanation: Feedback is the response given by the receiver, which tells the nurse whether the message was clearly understood. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: A nurse finds a toddler in an oxygen tent with damp clothes and cool skin. What should you do first?

options.A: Change the damp clothing and check the tent cooling settings
options.B: Administer an antipyretic medication for potential fever
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow rate on the wall flowmeter
options.D: Remove the child from the tent and place a nasal cannula

explanation: Moisture inside the tent can get clothes wet, which makes the child cold fast. Dressing them in dry clothes keeps them cozy and safe!

question: What is the primary purpose of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: Recruiting new nursing staff for the facility
options.B: Monitoring performance and taking corrective action
options.C: Assigning daily bedside duties to junior nurses
options.D: Drafting the annual financial budget for the hospital

explanation: Controlling is primarily about tracking actual work against set plans and fixing mistakes when things go wrong. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why are social programs like senior centers so helpful for older adults?

options.A: They provide free prescription drugs for chronic illnesses
options.B: They offer round-the-clock intensive nursing care
options.C: They replace the need for regular medical checkups
options.D: They reduce isolation and promote mental well-being

explanation: Getting together for social activities helps seniors make friends, stay happy, and chase away loneliness.

question: What is the most common exercise used to strengthen the pelvic floor without surgery?

options.A: Abdominal crunches
options.B: Kegel exercises
options.C: Quadriceps extensions
options.D: Hamstring stretches

explanation: Easy peasy! Kegels are the classic squeeze-and-release exercises that build great pelvic strength.

question: What is a key food safety practice you should teach your outpatients?

options.A: Eating leftover food without reheating it
options.B: Storing perishable foods at room temperature for days
options.C: Rinsing all raw meat with warm water before cutting
options.D: Keeping raw meats away from fresh vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Separating raw meats from ready-to-eat foods stops dangerous germs from spreading in the kitchen.

question: What administrative penalty can the Nursing and Midwifery Council impose for drug law violations?

options.A: A temporary transfer to a different medical department
options.B: Requiring the nurse to attend a basic computer class
options.C: Suspension or revocation of the nursing practicing license
options.D: Mandatory promotion to a hospital management position

explanation: Professional regulatory bodies protect the public by removing the licenses of unsafe practitioners. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h8)

question: What temperature must a standard freezer maintain to keep food safe?
explanation: A temperature of -18°C or lower keeps food frozen solid and stops bacteria from growing. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h5)

question: Why is chronic kidney disease an important thing to note when taking a patient's blood history?

options.A: It triggers sudden and uncontrollable blood clotting
options.B: Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin, causing anaemia
options.C: It causes the liver to stop storing iron completely
options.D: Kidney failure immediately destroys all white blood cells

explanation: Healthy kidneys make erythropoietin, the hormone that tells the bone marrow to build red blood cells. When kidneys fail, that hormone drops, leading to anaemia.

question: A patient is experiencing acute withdrawal tremors and confusion. Which nursing diagnosis should be your top priority?

options.A: Ineffective Health Maintenance
options.B: Chronic Low Self-Esteem
options.C: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.D: Risk for Injury

explanation: Correct! With tremors and confusion, keeping the patient safe from falls, seizures, and self-harm is always the absolute first priority in nursing care.

question: What is the main job of white blood cells when an infection enters the body?

options.A: To defend the body by neutralizing foreign invaders
options.B: To transport oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To digest food and absorb nutrients
options.D: To regulate blood pressure and fluid balance

explanation: Your white blood cells are your body's frontline military defenders, always on patrol to hunt down and destroy invading germs.

question: What is the primary fluid environment surrounding the body's cells called?

options.A: Extracellular fluid
options.B: Intracellular fluid
options.C: Transcellular fluid
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Extracellular fluid surrounds the body's cells and forms the internal environment that must remain stable for cellular survival. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main reason we practice standard precautions in everyday nursing?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients and staff
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the patient's bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: To eliminate the need for documenting medication administration

explanation: Standard precautions are your trusty shield! They keep both you and your patients safe from passing germs back and forth during care.

question: A nurse notices that a disinfectant storage room has no windows or airflow. What immediate danger does this pose?

options.A: Rapid growth of bacterial spores inside the closed storage containers
options.B: Automatic expiration of every chemical bottle within twenty-four hours
options.C: Immediate freezing of all liquid disinfectants stored on the shelves
options.D: Accumulation of harmful chemical fumes leading to staff respiratory irritation

explanation: Good catch! Without proper ventilation, strong chemical vapors build up in the air and can make nursing staff very sick when they breathe them in.

question: How does child health directly improve when a family uses effective family planning methods?

options.A: The need for childhood immunizations is drastically reduced.
options.B: Children automatically develop stronger natural immunity to all infections.
options.C: Infants are born with a higher average birth weight without exception.
options.D: Resources can be better shared to prevent malnutrition and infant illness.

explanation: You got it! When births are well-spaced, parents can better invest time, money, and nutrition into each child, keeping them healthier and well-nourished.

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you first meet the patient and build trust?

options.A: Evaluation phase
options.B: Working phase
options.C: Orientation phase
options.D: Termination phase

explanation: Think of the orientation phase as your first introduction! It's where you say hello, explain your role, and start building that initial trust.

question: Why would a nurse choose the intradermal route for giving a medication?

options.A: Allergy and sensitivity testing
options.B: Large volume fluid replacement
options.C: Long-term antibiotic therapy
options.D: Rapid systemic pain relief

explanation: You've got this! Intradermal injections go just under the top layer of skin, which makes them perfect for checking things like TB or allergies. They aren't meant for fast whole-body treatment.

question: What is the main reason nurses use functional assessment tools in a rehab ward?

options.A: To calculate the exact date of hospital discharge
options.B: To measure how much assistance a patient needs with daily activities
options.C: To determine daily caloric requirements
options.D: To diagnose underlying genetic mutations

explanation: You got it! These tools help us clearly see how independent a patient is and track their progress over time.

question: Which of these is a very common hazard found right inside an older adult's home?

options.A: Bright overhead lighting in every room
options.B: Grab bars installed inside the shower
options.C: Low kitchen counters with wide open space
options.D: Loose scatter rugs and cluttered walkways

explanation: Simple things like loose rugs or blocked pathways are major tripping hazards that frequently lead to dangerous falls at home.

question: Which of these is NOT a good topic for patient education regarding dietary supplements?

options.A: Bringing all supplement containers to clinic appointments for review
options.B: Checking for valid NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels
options.C: How to manufacture herbal capsules at home in your kitchen
options.D: Reporting unusual side effects or symptoms to a healthcare provider

explanation: As nurses, we teach safety, checking labels, and reporting side effects—we definitely don't encourage brewing or making DIY pills at home!

question: A patient with a painful ankle gout flare says even the bedsheet touching the skin is agonizing. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Massage the ankle firmly to increase circulation and numb the area
options.B: Use a bed cradle to keep the linens elevated off the painful ankle
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around the room to break up the crystals
options.D: Apply a warm heating pad directly to the skin over the joint

explanation: A bed cradle is a simple device that keeps blankets lifted off the foot, giving immediate relief to an extremely tender joint.

question: Which major risk factor is most closely linked to oesophageal cancer?

options.A: Frequent bacterial throat infections
options.B: Chronic gastro-oesophageal reflux
options.C: Allergic reactions to dairy products
options.D: Regular consumption of very spicy food

explanation: Years of acid constantly splashing up changes the delicate cells lining the lower oesophagus, which can eventually pave the way for cancer.

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: NAFDAC
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: National Youth Service Corps
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education

explanation: You've got this! NAFDAC is our watchdog, keeping watch over how drugs are made, imported, and sold across Nigeria.

question: What is likely to happen if a hospital sets its DRF mark-up to zero percent?

options.A: The pharmacy will gradually lose purchasing power due to inflation and waste, leading to stock-outs
options.B: Patients will buy more drugs because they are cheaper, making the fund richer
options.C: The hospital will save money on administrative costs and paperwork
options.D: The government will send extra money every month to maintain the exact same inventory level

explanation: Without a small mark-up to cover waste and inflation, your capital gradually shrinks until you can no longer afford to restock.

question: Which vaccine is given in adolescent health programs to protect against cervical cancer later in life?

options.A: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine
options.B: Oral polio vaccine
options.C: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid vaccine

explanation: Exactly! Giving the HPV vaccine to adolescents is a powerful preventive tool against the strains of the virus that cause cervical cancer.

question: What happens to the placental membrane as pregnancy nears full term?

options.A: It completely disappears to let blood mix directly
options.B: It thins out to allow easier exchange of substances
options.C: It turns into hard bone tissue to support the cord
options.D: It grows thicker to protect the fetus from infections

explanation: As the baby grows and needs more nourishment, the membrane gets thinner and thinner so oxygen and nutrients can pass through much faster. Smart design! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h2)

question: During a vaginal exam, you feel that the baby's skull bones are severely overlapping and jammed tight. What condition might this suggest?

options.A: Premature rupture of membranes
options.B: Normal rapid crowning
options.C: Normal painless descent
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Severe, tight overlapping is a sign that the head is struggling to fit through a tight birth canal—a condition we call cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD). Keep this red flag in mind for clinicals!

question: You are managing a patient with acute PPH. Which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Checking vital signs every 5 to 15 minutes
options.B: Instructing the patient to walk around to encourage drainage
options.C: Calling for help from the multidisciplinary team right away
options.D: Setting up large-bore IV lines for fluid replacement

explanation: Never let a bleeding, shock-prone patient walk around! That can instantly cause her blood pressure to bottom out and lead to a collapse. Strict bed rest is a must.

question: What should a nurse do when a patient refuses to take a prescribed oral medication?

options.A: Document the refusal and notify the prescribing doctor
options.B: Hide the crushed pill inside sweet food without telling them
options.C: Force the medication gently by holding the patient's jaw
options.D: Leave the pill on the bedside table for them to take later

explanation: Competent patients have the right to refuse treatment, and the care team must be informed to adjust the plan. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the most critical dietary instruction for a patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease?

options.A: Maintain strict, lifelong elimination of all foods containing gluten
options.B: Avoid dairy products only during acute episodes of abdominal pain
options.C: Increase fiber intake temporarily until bowel villi fully regrow
options.D: Reduce fat intake to prevent steatorrhea during flare-ups

explanation: Celiac disease is a permanent condition requiring complete, lifelong removal of gluten to allow mucosal healing and prevent complications. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h8)

question: Which imaging test is best for getting a clear view of bone structures in the sinuses and ears?

options.A: Routine chest X-ray
options.B: Surface skin ultrasound
options.C: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

explanation: CT scans are fantastic at imaging hard bone, making them the top choice for looking at sinus walls and inner ear details.

question: Under Nigerian law, what is a specific rule public organizations must follow regarding employment?

options.A: They must provide free housing for all disabled citizens.
options.B: They must exempt disabled individuals from paying any taxes.
options.C: They must allocate at least 5% of their workforce positions to persons with disabilities.
options.D: They must fund private medical clinics in every rural community.

explanation: The law sets a helpful employment quota requiring public establishments to reserve a minimum of 5% of their jobs for qualified persons with disabilities.

question: To renew your nursing license later on, you need proof of ongoing learning. How do professional organizations usually help you get this?

options.A: By providing free textbooks for basic nursing school entrance exams
options.B: By granting automatic license renewals without any coursework
options.C: By offering structured workshops and continuing education courses
options.D: By paying the state licensing board fees directly for the nurse

explanation: Professional organizations provide approved educational programs and workshops that give you the exact learning credits you need for license renewal.

question: How does your blood protect your body against germs and infections?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells
options.B: By filtering toxins directly through the skin
options.C: By lowering blood pressure during an illness
options.D: By circulating white blood cells and antibodies

explanation: Exactly! Your bloodstream acts like a highway, rushing white blood cells and antibodies straight to wherever germs are trying to attack.

question: What is the main point of cough etiquette in a busy clinic waiting area?

options.A: To contain respiratory droplets at the source and stop germ spread
options.B: To prevent the buildup of dust particles on furniture
options.C: To cure patients who suffer from chronic lung diseases
options.D: To eliminate the need for healthcare workers to wear face masks

explanation: Exactly! Catching those droplets early stops airborne bugs from floating around and infecting everyone in the waiting room.

question: Why should standard cloth or fabric tailors' tapes be avoided in clinical practice?

options.A: They only measure in inches rather than centimeters
options.B: They are too expensive for community clinics
options.C: They stretch over time and give false readings
options.D: They dissolve easily when exposed to skin moisture

explanation: Fabric stretches with repeated pulling, which ruins the accuracy required for precise health tracking. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which blood test helps prove that a patient recently had a strep infection?

options.A: Liver function panel
options.B: Anti-Streptolysin O (ASO) titer
options.C: Complete blood count (CBC)
options.D: Fast blood sugar level

explanation: An elevated ASO titer is the specific lab test doctors use to check if strep antibodies are floating around after a recent infection.

question: Why do some women delay seeking medical care for incomplete abortions in local communities?

options.A: Automatic recovery without intervention in nearly all septic cases
options.B: Lack of interest in recovering from physical weakness or bleeding
options.C: Strict government regulations that ban women from leaving their homes
options.D: Fear of social stigma, legal repercussions, and judgment from healthcare workers

explanation: True. Fear of harsh treatment by hospital staff or society stops many women from seeking timely care.

question: Why are contaminated water sources such a huge public health worry?

options.A: They turn into live animal nests within a few hours
options.B: They stop antibiotics from working on skin cuts
options.C: They can quickly spread water germs to a whole lot of people at once
options.D: They automatically kill all the good bacteria in your tummy

explanation: Since everyone drinks water, a dirty water source can easily cause a massive community outbreak in no time.

question: What is the main job of the water-seal chamber in a chest drainage setup?

options.A: To deliver humidified oxygen directly into the pleural space
options.B: To allow air to escape from the chest while preventing outside air from entering
options.C: To apply high-pressure suction to reinflate collapsed tissue
options.D: To measure the total volume of blood lost over twenty-four hours

explanation: It acts like a smart one-way valve—letting trapped air bubble out, but never letting room air sneak back in. Brilliant piece of bedside engineering!

question: Which mistake during a cervical swab can ruin the lab result?

options.A: Explaining the testing procedure to the patient too early
options.B: Using a plastic speculum instead of a cold metal one
options.C: Allowing the patient to empty their bladder before the exam
options.D: Leaving excess mucus on the cervix before taking the sample

explanation: You got it! Too much mucus or discharge blocks the cells, making it impossible for the lab tech to read the sample accurately.

question: What is the main goal of family planning in public health?

options.A: Allowing individuals to choose the timing and spacing of children
options.B: Forcing families to limit their total number of offspring to two
options.C: Eliminating population growth completely across all developing nations
options.D: Providing free medical care exclusively for newborn infants

explanation: You got it! Family planning is all about giving people the freedom to decide when and how often to have children, which keeps both parents and babies healthy.

question: Which major blood vessel feeds oxygen-rich blood to the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine?

options.A: Superior mesenteric artery
options.B: Celiac trunk
options.C: Inferior mesenteric artery
options.D: Renal artery

explanation: The superior mesenteric artery is the main lifeline branching off the aorta to supply the small intestine and upper colon. Keep crushing it!

question: Which of these is a common traditional widowhood practice that involves keeping a widow away from others?

options.A: Permanent physical exile from the community
options.B: Mandatory immediate relocation to another state
options.C: Confinement in a secluded room for an extended period
options.D: Ban on speaking to any male healthcare worker

explanation: Many traditions require a grieving widow to stay locked away from public view for weeks or months as part of the mourning customs.

question: What is the purpose of a cough stress test during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check if coughing triggers a bladder spasm
options.B: To test the strength of the patient's respiratory muscles
options.C: To measure lung capacity while the patient lies flat
options.D: To observe if physical pressure causes immediate urine leakage

explanation: By asking the patient to cough, the clinician can watch directly to see if pressure causes any accidental leakage.

question: A patient comes in with a 'buffalo hump' of fat, a round belly, and purple stretch marks on their skin. Which condition matches these signs?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Cushing's disease
options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Diabetes insipidus

explanation: These classic changes happen when the body is flooded with too much cortisol. In Cushing's disease, this is often kicked off by a tiny pituitary tumor pushing out extra ACTH.

question: A patient complains that their prescribed diet cuts out all their favorite cultural dishes and feels impossible. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient they have no choice and must strictly obey the prescription
options.B: Work with the patient to find healthy substitutes and modify their favorite cultural meals
options.C: Ignore the complaint since food preferences do not affect health outcomes
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until they adjust to the new menu

explanation: That's patient-centered care! Respecting their culture and tweaking their favorite meals makes it much more likely they will stick to the plan.

question: What is one of the most common causes of medication errors on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Distractions and interruptions during preparation
options.B: Writing patient names clearly in black ink
options.C: Performing three checks against the prescription order
options.D: Asking patients to state their date of birth

explanation: Noise and interruptions break your focus. When drawing up meds or checking doses, try to find a quiet zone to avoid silly mistakes!

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic drooling, tearing up, peeing frequently, and having muscle twitches after spraying the farm. What is this?

options.A: Sedative overdose from sleeping pills
options.B: Cholinergic poisoning from organophosphates
options.C: Caustic poisoning from swallowed acid
options.D: Opioid poisoning from strong painkillers

explanation: Correct! Remember the DUMBELS sign (drooling, urination, muscle twitching, etc.)—it points straight to organophosphate poisoning.

question: Which emotional challenge is commonly experienced by family caregivers of patients with degenerative disorders?

options.A: Complete immunity to daily stress
options.B: Caregiver burnout and exhaustion
options.C: Instant recovery of physical strength
options.D: Sudden loss of all personal memories

explanation: Providing round-the-clock care for a progressively worsening condition can heavily drain family members, making caregiver support a vital part of nursing. You're learning fast!

question: A student with asthma starts wheezing badly during sports. What should the school nurse do first?

options.A: Send the student home immediately without any medical assessment
options.B: Tell the student to run faster to clear their airways naturally
options.C: Assess the student and administer the prescribed rescue inhaler
options.D: Wait until the end of the school day to notify the parents

explanation: You got it! The nurse needs to quickly check the student and give their emergency rescue inhaler as outlined in their care plan.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four key elements needed to prove malpractice?

options.A: Guilt
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Breach

explanation: To prove malpractice, you need duty, breach, causation, and damages. 'Guilt' belongs in criminal law, not civil malpractice cases.

question: Why is it smart to call the receiving hospital on the phone before sending an emergency patient?

options.A: To confirm the exact home address of the ambulance driver
options.B: To ask the doctor on duty for permission to use their hospital ambulance
options.C: To ensure the receiving team can prepare equipment and space for the patient
options.D: To negotiate the medical bills before the patient arrives at the gate

explanation: A quick heads-up phone call lets the hospital prep a bed, oxygen, or blood products before the ambulance even rolls through their gates.

question: What is a major infectious cause of scar tissue that leads to ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Urinary tract infection
options.B: Bacterial vaginosis
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease causes inflammation and scarring in the fallopian tubes, blocking the normal path of a fertilized egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h3)

question: How do day care services benefit family caregivers directly?

options.A: By offering financial loans for business start-ups
options.B: By reducing caregiver burnout through reliable respite
options.C: By permanently taking over full parental responsibilities
options.D: By providing free housing facilities for the whole family

explanation: Reliable daytime care gives parents and family caregivers time to work or rest, preventing severe physical and emotional exhaustion. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why is it important to involve male leaders when advocating for family planning in rural Nigerian settings?

options.A: Men are the only individuals who experience pregnancy complications.
options.B: Men often hold decision-making power regarding household health choices and finances.
options.C: Women are legally prohibited from visiting health clinics alone.
options.D: Male leaders personally distribute contraceptives to all villagers.

explanation: In many patriarchal rural settings, men control household resources and approval, making their engagement vital for successful family planning adoption. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h5)

question: A nurse wants to measure patient satisfaction using options from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree'. Which format should she use?

options.A: Likert scale
options.B: Open-ended essay
options.C: Dichotomous checklist
options.D: Biographical interview

explanation: A Likert scale is designed specifically to measure attitudes and agreement levels across a multi-point scale. Great job learning the research tools!

question: Why is community participation essential in health promotion?

options.A: People must be involved in identifying their own health needs and solutions
options.B: Foreign donors require it before releasing any funds
options.C: It ensures that nurses do not have to work in rural areas
options.D: It guarantees that the government will provide free vehicles

explanation: Active community involvement ensures that health programs actually match what the people need and care about, leading to better success rates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: If an elderly patient keeps falling at home, what should be your very first assessment priority?

options.A: The patient's long-term childhood medical history
options.B: The brand of television in the living room
options.C: Environmental hazards and walking paths in the home
options.D: Family members' personal employment schedules

explanation: Exactly! Checking the immediate living space for physical dangers like loose rugs or poor lighting is the quickest way to uncover why someone keeps tripping.

question: What is the main job of the climbing fibers as they enter the cerebellar cortex?

options.A: Transport cerebrospinal fluid through the ventricles
options.B: Provide powerful excitatory input for motor learning
options.C: Produce myelin for the parallel nerve fibers
options.D: Inhibit the activity of the deep cerebellar nuclei

explanation: Climbing fibers wrap right around Purkinje cells to deliver strong signals that help fine-tune your movements when learning a new physical skill. You're mastering neuroanatomy step by step!

question: What is an effective nursing action to address patient demands for unnecessary injections?

options.A: Administering sterile water to trick the patient safely
options.B: Obeying the patient demand immediately to avoid arguing
options.C: Refusing to provide any medical care until the patient leaves
options.D: Explaining the benefits of oral medications and reassuring the patient

explanation: Patient education helps correct the misconception that oral drugs are weak, reducing unnecessary injection requests. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is a referral in the context of family planning?

options.A: Directing a client to another facility when needs exceed current capacity
options.B: Ordering a new brand of oral contraceptive pills from the pharmacy
options.C: Discharging a client completely from the healthcare system
options.D: Scheduling a routine return visit for the same clinic next month

explanation: A referral happens when a client needs specialized care or resources that the current primary facility cannot provide. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: A community nurse notices women in a village avoiding breast screening due to cultural fears. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Report the village residents to local government authorities for non-compliance
options.B: Insist that screening is mandatory under all circumstances
options.C: Ignore the cultural beliefs and hand out clinical pamphlets silently
options.D: Provide culturally sensitive health education and address community fears openly

explanation: Spot on! Building trust through gentle, respectful conversations and addressing fears openly is always the best nursing approach for community health.

question: What should you warn your patient about right before you start a bladder irrigation?

options.A: Immediate drowsiness and heavy sleepiness
options.B: A strong urge to urinate or mild cramping
options.C: Numbness spreading down both upper legs
options.D: A sharp burning sensation in the lower back

explanation: No need to alarm them—just let them know that filling the bladder naturally tricks the body into feeling like it really needs to pee!

question: How is child trafficking different from regular help on a family farm?

options.A: Trafficking always involves coercion and exploitation
options.B: Trafficking only happens in urban city centers
options.C: Normal labor is strictly illegal for all minors
options.D: Normal labor pays a much higher daily wage

explanation: While helping out with family chores or learning a trade can be safe, trafficking relies on deceit, force, and taking advantage of a child against their will.

question: A patient is completely bedridden from a muscle disorder. Which bone problem are they most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of red blood cells
options.B: Pathological bone fractures from decreased density
options.C: Involuntary muscle hypertrophy in the lower limbs
options.D: Drastic permanent height gain from spinal decompression

explanation: Bones need weight and pressure to stay strong. Staying in bed stops that pressure, making bones weak and fragile.

question: What is a common misconception about using opioids for pain management in palliative patients?

options.A: They always cause severe allergic reactions
options.B: They stop working completely after the first dose
options.C: They can only be given through intravenous lines
options.D: They will inevitably cause immediate respiratory arrest

explanation: When opioids are carefully adjusted for pain, dangerous breathing slowdowns are rare because the body builds tolerance to that side effect. Don't let the fear of opioids fool you!

question: Which imaging scan is best for spotting hippocampal scarring in psychomotor epilepsy?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Standard skull X-ray
options.C: Bone density scan
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: An MRI gives a clear, high-resolution picture of soft brain tissues, making it the top choice for finding tiny scars or shrinking in the hippocampus. Great job! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h4)

question: What does the FEFO inventory rule stand for in vaccine management?

options.A: Fastest Entry, Fastest Out
options.B: First Expire, First Out
options.C: Freeze Early, Freeze Often
options.D: Final Evaluation, Final Order

explanation: FEFO ensures that vaccines nearing their expiration date are used before newer supplies to prevent wastage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: Which set of vital signs shows that a patient's circulation is collapsing from an allergy?

options.A: Low heart rate and low blood pressure
options.B: High heart rate and low blood pressure
options.C: Low heart rate and high blood pressure
options.D: High heart rate and high blood pressure

explanation: As blood pressure drops, the heart beats much faster to try and make up for it and keep blood flowing.

question: Which breathing sound tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway obstruction?

options.A: Crackles
options.B: Wheezing
options.C: Friction rub
options.D: Stridor

explanation: Stridor is that high-pitched, strained sound you hear when air is struggling to push past a blockage in the upper airway. You can often hear it without a stethoscope!

question: What is almost always the very first test a nurse or doctor will order for a woman of childbearing age with secondary amenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain MRI
options.B: Endometrial biopsy
options.C: Karyotype analysis
options.D: Pregnancy test

explanation: Pregnancy is the most common reason a period stops, so we always check this first before running more complex tests!

question: Why should hospital management always consult frontline ward nurses when planning a new ward layout?

options.A: Nurses know practical workflow details like storage bottlenecks and blind spots
options.B: Nurses will personally fund the construction of the new nursing station
options.C: Nurses are legally required to sign off on all architectural blueprints
options.D: Nurses decide the overall construction budget for the entire hospital

explanation: You are the one working in the space every day! Consulting nurses helps catch practical issues—like where supplies should go—that architects might easily miss.

question: What is a major benefit of putting a newborn straight onto the mother's chest for skin-to-skin contact?

options.A: It stabilizes the infant's body temperature and heart rate
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for vitamin K injections
options.C: It speeds up the closure of the umbilical cord vessels
options.D: It prevents the occurrence of physiological jaundice

explanation: Mum's chest is like a natural incubator! It helps steady the baby's breathing, heart rate, and keeps them nice and warm.

question: What is a major structural difference between sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways?

options.A: Sympathetic fibers never use ganglia to pass signals along.
options.B: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers are always much longer than postganglionic fibers.
options.C: Parasympathetic nerves only exit through the lumbar spinal cord.
options.D: Parasympathetic ganglia are usually located close to or inside the target organs.

explanation: Because parasympathetic fibers travel a long way from the brain or lower spine before reaching their destination, their relay stations (ganglia) sit right near or inside the target organ walls.

question: What do spoon-shaped or concave nails often tell you about a patient?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Chronic low blood oxygen
options.C: A fungal nail infection
options.D: Poor peripheral circulation

explanation: Well done! When nails dip inward like a little spoon (called koilonychia), it's a classic clue that the patient might be struggling with low iron.

question: Why is getting support from religious and traditional leaders important for youth health programs?

options.A: It reduces community stigma and builds adult support for youth health initiatives
options.B: It eliminates the need for trained nurses in rural health posts
options.C: It makes health facilities exempt from paying local taxes
options.D: It gives leaders the authority to prescribe medications to teenagers

explanation: When community leaders understand and back the program, it eases resistance and helps parents feel good about their teens receiving care.

question: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 8 to 11 breaths per minute
options.B: 22 to 30 breaths per minute
options.C: 12 to 20 breaths per minute
options.D: 35 to 40 breaths per minute

explanation: A normal, healthy adult at rest breathes between 12 and 20 times every minute. Rates outside this range can indicate underlying respiratory or metabolic problems. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is it important to treat chronic pain promptly in a physically disabled patient?

options.A: Pain always causes immediate permanent paralysis
options.B: Untreated pain speeds up the digestive system dangerously
options.C: Pain can limit their ability to participate in rehabilitation therapy
options.D: Pain medication is the only way to prevent skin ulcers

explanation: When pain is poorly controlled, patients cannot engage in vital physical therapy exercises needed to maintain mobility. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Emergency involves acute damage to target organs, while urgency does not.
options.B: Urgency occurs only in children, whereas emergency affects adults.
options.C: Emergency can be safely treated at home with herbal teas.
options.D: Urgency involves higher blood pressure numbers than emergency.

explanation: Spot on! An emergency means high blood pressure is actively damaging vital organs like the brain or heart, requiring immediate medical care.

question: A patient sitting in a wheelchair for long hours is most likely to develop pressure sores on which specific area?

options.A: Ischial tuberosities
options.B: Occipital bone
options.C: Bridge of the nose
options.D: Anterior patella

explanation: The ischial tuberosities are simply your sitting bones! When a patient sits for too long, these bones take the heavy brunt of the body weight. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: How does nursing in the community differ from working in a big hospital ward?

options.A: Home nurses rely heavily on resourcefulness and critical thinking in the community.
options.B: Home nurses have direct access to immediate physician support at all times.
options.C: Hospital nurses perform fewer physical assessments than community nurses.
options.D: Hospital nurses manage fewer complex chronic conditions than home nurses.

explanation: You got it! Without hospital equipment and doctors right next door, home care nurses have to trust their training, think on their feet, and solve problems creatively.

question: Why is it important to rotate where you stick daily patches or put long-term creams?

options.A: It stops the medication from expiring inside the body.
options.B: It keeps the skin color even across the whole body.
options.C: It ensures the medicine travels to all four limbs equally.
options.D: It prevents skin irritation, breakdown, and irritation from repetitive use in one spot.

explanation: Giving the skin a break by moving patches around prevents irritation, breakdown, and keeps the skin healthy enough to absorb the medicine properly.

question: A nurse is teaching a client with chronic venous insufficiency how to care for themselves daily. What advice fits best?

options.A: Elevate your legs above the level of your heart several times a day.
options.B: Avoid wearing compression stockings during your normal daytime hours.
options.C: Stand in place for long periods to keep your leg muscles active.
options.D: Cross your legs at the knees whenever sitting down in a chair.

explanation: Gravity is your friend here! Propping those legs up high helps fluid drain back toward the heart instead of pooling at the ankles.

question: Which hormone acts like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping its muscles calm and preventing early contractions?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: You got it! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles, keeping the uterus nice and quiet throughout the pregnancy journey.

question: Why must adverse event reporting systems in hospitals be non-punitive?

options.A: To encourage staff to report mistakes without fear of harsh punishment
options.B: To allow doctors to bypass hospital management rules freely
options.C: To ensure that nurses never have to document anything in writing
options.D: To reduce the need for buying emergency resuscitation equipment

explanation: If staff fear punishment, they will hide errors instead of reporting them, preventing the hospital from learning and improving safety. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h4)
